title: Arkret Recovery Policy
description: Normative grammar for an account's PCR recovery policy. Bound through signed control events to one exact AccountId and its local unique PCR lineage; receivers reject recovery and pcr_recovery device authorization whose proof family, threshold or optional DID-root factor is not allowed by the currently accepted policy.

version.description: Monotonically increasing counter scoped by the exact account_id. Receivers MUST reject a publish whose version is not strictly greater than the currently accepted policy.

supersedes_id.description: Predecessor policy_id. Null only for the genesis policy of an exact account.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier the policy applies to. Cross-domain proofs MUST fail.

allowed_proof_kinds.description: Which proof families authorize PCR device re-entry. did_root is optional and revocable; omitting it guarantees current DID control alone cannot recover this account-local lineage.

publication_authorization_rules.description: Signed deterministic projection inputs for PCR recovery publication. Exactly one rule per allowed proof kind; a revoked policy carries an empty array.

threshold.description: Threshold-recovery configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'threshold_recovery'.

k.description: Minimum share count required to reconstruct the recovery secret. MUST be >= 2; threshold=1 is forbidden because it collapses to a single-holder bearer.

vss_root_commitment.description: Optional VSS root commitment binding all shares' polynomial commitments. SHOULD be present for Feldman / Pedersen schemes.

reshare_policy.description: Proactive secret sharing / re-share cadence. Holders MUST be able to refresh shares without reconstructing the secret. Implementations SHOULD re-share at least once per `max_share_age_seconds`.

device_quorum.description: Device-quorum configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'device_quorum'.

authorization_verification_method.description: Exact verification method authorized by this accepted PCR recovery-policy rule. DID-root methods are valid only for proof_kind=did_root; service and quorum rules derive from their own accepted policy basis.

trusted_recovery_services.description: Recovery services explicitly declared in the principal's DID Document (or sovereign trust seal). Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'trusted_recovery_service'.

recovery_keys.description: Recovery signing keys this principal authorizes for 'recovery_unlock' proofs and for the single publication signature produced after 'threshold_recovery' secret reconstruction. Each entry binds a verification method (24-word Recovery Key derived signing key, or hardware-released equivalent) to the principal. A recovery_unlock proof's recovery_secret_ref, and a threshold_recovery publication rule's issuer set, MUST resolve to active entries in this array; the proof signature MUST verify under the selected entry's public key. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains either 'recovery_unlock' or 'threshold_recovery'. See identity/key-management.md §7.5.2 and §8, identity/security-transactions.md §2, and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.

recovery_key_agreements.description: Backup-only HPKE recipient keys. These entries are cryptographically and semantically distinct from recovery_keys[] signing keys. key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref resolves only here in the envelope's referenced accepted policy, never to a DID Document-only key agreement or a recovery signing verification_method.

approval_requirement.description: Two-person rule / cooldown enforcement layered on top of cryptographic proofs.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wall-clock window between recovery announcement and effective key change. Receivers MUST reject control-stream Events whose accepted_at is earlier than announcement_at + cooldown_seconds.

announcement_required.description: When true, recovery MUST be announced on the principal control stream and visible to authorized devices before effective key change.

audit.description: Where the recovery strand MUST emit auditable records (recovery announcement, holder participation, completion receipt).

receipt_required.description: When true, recovery completion MUST produce a ak.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 record.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the authorized issuer: founding device after genesis; current-generation accepted device for later updates; identity root for re-anchor; or a coordinator satisfying the superseded policy quorum. Receivers resolve this semantic authority from accepted principal-control state, not from arbitrary DID Document membership.

signature.description: base64url signature over UTF8('ak.identity.recovery_policy.signature.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of all present top-level policy members except auth_data. The closed policy shape fixes the projection; absent optional members are omitted and null is retained only where the schema explicitly admits null.

recovery_policy_set_payload.description: Canonical ak.policy.set payload for recovery-policy publication. policy_id MUST equal value.policy_id; state and reason are intentionally unavailable on this operation.

recovery_policy_publish_request.description: Recovery policy publication through the ordinary first-publication Event ingress. Cross-field validation additionally requires payload.policy_id=value.policy_id and actor/scope/lease to bind value.account_id's exact Principal Control Realm.

recovery_key_entry.description: A recovery signing key the principal authorizes for 'recovery_unlock' proofs and post-reconstruction 'threshold_recovery' publication signatures. The verification_method is the stable recovery_secret_ref and publication-rule issuer; public_key_multibase carries the actual signing public key so principals do not depend on a DID Document verificationMethod. key_agreement_ref pairs this signer with a distinct backup-only recovery_key_agreements[] entry.

verification_method.description: DID URL (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-1`) identifying this recovery signing key. This is the value a recovery_unlock proof carries in recovery_secret_ref / verification_method and a threshold_recovery publication rule carries in issuers[].verification_method; it MUST be unique within recovery_keys[].

public_key_multibase.description: Multikey for the recovery proof signature algorithm. MUST NOT equal or be converted into the paired HPKE key.

key_agreement_ref.description: MUST identify exactly one non-revoked recovery_key_agreements[] entry in the same policy.

signature_algorithm.description: Signature algorithm used by the recovery key. Values mirror active signature-alg-registry rows; ML-DSA-65 use additionally requires the corresponding PQ-capable implementation profile.

not_before.description: Earliest instant this recovery key may authorize a recovery_unlock proof or threshold_recovery publication signature.

expires_at.description: Instant after which this recovery key MUST NOT authorize a recovery_unlock proof or threshold_recovery publication signature.

revoked_at.description: When set, the entry is revoked from this instant onward and MUST NOT satisfy any recovery_unlock proof or threshold_recovery publication signature whose binding time is at or after it.

recovery_key_agreement_entry.description: Dedicated X25519 HPKE recipient for key-backup envelopes. It cannot verify recovery_unlock or authorize DID/Event operations.

key_agreement_ref.description: Stable identifier used by key-backup encryption.recipient_key_ref.

recovery_policy_summary.description: Read-model summary of the currently accepted recovery policy. `policy` carries the original ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object when the service can disclose it to the caller.

acceptance_basis_ref.description: Immutable accepted CBS basis whose control state commits this exact recovery policy version.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple equivalent to `{policy_id, policy_version: version}`. When present, it MUST match policy_id/version.

policy.description: Full accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object. Omitted only when the caller is authorized to learn that a policy exists but not to receive holder/share details.

control_frontier.description: Optional account control-stream frontier under which the active policy was observed.

recovery_policy_active_outcome.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.resource.get.v1. `active_policy=null` is a successful read meaning no accepted recovery policy currently exists for the resolved exact account.

account_id.description: Resolved exact account. Required when the request used an explicit account_id selector; SHOULD be present on all authenticated reads.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple for the active policy. MUST be absent or null-equivalent when active_policy is null, and MUST match active_policy.policy_id/version when active_policy is present.

recovery_policy_publish_outcome.description: Response for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish.v1 after accepting a ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 publish or rotation.

acceptance_basis_ref.description: Immutable accepted CBS basis whose control state commits this exact recovery policy version.

recovery_share_holder.description: Closed identity carrier for a recovery-share holder. A holder is either an independently verified personal principal or an explicitly authorized custodial service; v1 defines no hardware-module branch.

holder_principal_id.description: Stable principal core of a personal share holder. The holder does not inherit any business capability of the recovered account.

holder_service_id.description: Stable service core of a custodial recovery service accepted by the recovery policy.
